title: Boats to Save People
summary: Given an array of people's weights where each element represents the weight of the i-th person, determine the minimum number of boats required to save all the people.
statement: Given an array of people's weights where each element represents the weight of the i-th person, determine the minimum number of boats required to save all the people. Each boat can carry a maximum of two people, with the condition that the combined weight of the people in a boat does not exceed the boat's weight limit.
constraints: Each boat carries at most two people with combined weight at most limit.
hints: The heaviest remaining person must take a boat; pairing them with the lightest is optimal whenever feasible.
Always remove right; also remove left if their sum fits; increment boats.
If the lightest cannot pair with the heaviest nobody can; if they can, using the lightest preserves heavier partners for later.
editorial: If the lightest cannot pair with the heaviest nobody can; if they can, using the lightest preserves heavier partners for later.

tests.explanation: The optimal pairing uses three boats.
